lesson-intro.text: Three hills, one behind another. The one in front hides the feet of the others, and that is what makes a flat page look deep. Watch them line up, then let your own hills roll.

ground.text: The ground is one straight line. Draw it left to right along the bottom.

back-hill.text: The hill at the back is a wide arch. Leave a gap at its top for a trunk.

second-hill.text: The next hill arches up on the right, back down to the ground.

front-hill.text: One long arch across the front, corner to corner. It cuts over both hills.

left-tree.text: A pine stands in the gap. Short trunk first, then the spiky shape above it.

right-tree.text: The other pine is smaller, over on the second hill. Trunk, then spikes.

sun.text: Last, a plain circle high in the sky, clear of everything.

front-hill-color.text: Color the front hill dark green.

green-color.text: The hill on the right and both pines are green.

far-hill-color.text: The far hill on the left is pale green.

sun-trunks-color.text: The sun is yellow and the two trunks are brown.

lesson-outro.text: Three hills, and anyone can tell which one is nearest. That is depth, on a flat page.
